companion_apps.notes: Version 3.6.6 (versionCode 2127) was checked statically in the November 15 follow-up. Its React Native bundle contains all four Nano UUIDs in this spec. That corroborates identifiers only; the COBS/proto2 mapping comes from Anova's official Nano source, not from this string check.

identity.notes: The reference client keys the connection on the host Bluetooth device. Address type and stability are not established. DeviceInfo defines a serial field, but its read is not implemented in the reference client and no real serial may be logged or published.

methods.notes: The official client filters on this service and compares advertisement UUIDs case-insensitively. It chooses the first match; a production client should let the owner confirm the cooker before any heater write.

identification.notes: Require this advertised custom service, then confirm TX, RX and ASYNC after connecting. A third-party 2019 capture advertised the name Nano, but the official client matches the service and does not require that name. Do not use the name alone to distinguish a Nano from other Anova generations.

device.name: Anova Precision Cooker Nano
device.notes:
The BLE Nano uses one custom service with TX, RX and ASYNC characteristics. Commands have a two-byte domain/type header followed by an optional proto2 payload, then the entire logical packet is COBS-encoded and terminated by one zero delimiter. TX writes are split into at most 20-byte chunks in the official client. RX responses are reassembled; ASYNC is subscribed but its payload schema is not decoded by that client.
Normal operations use domain 0x00. Set/get target, get sensors, set/get unit, start/stop, set/get timer and get firmware are the demonstrated subset. The timer is MINUTES in the executable method, README and interactive prompts; a source-file top comment saying seconds is an internal documentation error, not a wire fact. Target temperature uses the current unit at scale 10. Sensors each carry their own unit and scale; never divide every sensor by 10.
SCOPE: this is the BLE Precision Cooker Nano. It is not the Mini's JSON/Base64 protocol, the original cooker's CR-terminated ASCII protocol on FFE0/FFE1, Nano 3.0/Wi-Fi models, later Mini/Lite hardware, or Anova cloud APIs. The original cooker's fixed PIN and the Mini's explicit host-pairing and reset instructions are not inherited.

openness.notes: The cached web command/protobuf tables conflict with the executable source. They assign configuration domain 0x01 and different opcodes, while the actual schema and client use configuration domain 0x00. This spec follows the pinned executable schema and records the conflict rather than sending the web-only values. No bulk transfer, reset, message-spoof or firmware command is declared.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The service is advertised for scanning, but no physical pairing-mode procedure or window was recovered.

exclusivity.notes: The official source does not state a PIN, bonding workflow, application key, central limit or bond capacity.
exclusivity.recovery: Close other clients and retry a read-only connection and get_temperature_unit. Do not invent a PIN, borrow a sibling model's pairing hold, or issue reset/bulk-domain writes to force rebinding.

pairing.notes: Pairing is an open question, not a hidden fixed-PIN or app-key flow. The official client connects and subscribes without demonstrating whether an unbonded link can complete every command.

unpair.clears: Unknown; no Nano-specific bond-removal procedure was recovered.
unpair.notes: Do not infer that host-side Forget clears device state, or that a factory reset is required. Actual bonding and reconnect behavior needs hardware.

safety_advisory.detail: Use only a correctly installed cooker with the water and vessel conditions required by its own vendor instructions. No authentic Nano manual was acquired, so this spec supplies no safe temperature range, water-depth rule or unattended-use claim. Read the temperature unit before every setpoint, preserve every sensor's own unit and scale, and never trust the reference client's optimistic local cooking flag or an arbitrary response as proof of a state change. A dedicated client should expose stop_cooking as recovery, serialize requests with timeouts and confirm attended stop behavior before testing a start. No generic entity action or stopped-state assumption is offered here.
safety_advisory.summary: This spec documents commands that can start and retarget an immersion heater. Start and setpoint require a deliberate action by a dedicated client; stop remains ordinary/non-advanced in the documentary catalogue.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi credential, application key or fixed PIN crosses the documented BLE protocol. Whether link-layer bonds are stored is unknown, so the empty list is not a claim that no bond state exists.

factory_reset.description: No authentic Nano quickstart manual was acquired. Do not reuse the Mini's ten-second top-button hold or the original cooker's Bluetooth button procedure for the Nano.
factory_reset.effect: No physical factory-reset procedure was recovered. The schema contains a bulk-domain system-reset message, but it is excluded from this spec and is not evidence of a safe owner reset flow or of what it clears.

methods.description: Scan for the Nano service, connect, subscribe to RX then ASYNC, read the temperature unit and serialize framed commands with timeouts. No heater write is part of setup.
methods.name: Direct BLE with RX/ASYNC subscriptions

steps.action: Power the Nano and scan for advertisements carrying 0e140000-0af1-4582-a242-773e63054c68, then connect.
Subscribe to RX 0e140002-0af1-4582-a242-773e63054c68 first and ASYNC 0e140003-0af1-4582-a242-773e63054c68 second.
A dedicated client must COBS-encode get_temperature_unit before sending it and wait for its IntegerValue response with a timeout; this spec provides no generic COBS handler.
steps.expect: A known UnitType establishes the current temperature unit. Unknown units are an error, not a Fahrenheit fallback. Do not send start_cooking during setup.

steps.action: Serialize subsequent commands one at a time, reassembling RX with the bounded rules in protocol_details.transport and preserving ASYNC bytes for future capture analysis rather than guessing a state object.

troubleshooting.fix: Stop sending, drain stale RX chunks, then retry get_temperature_unit with one request in flight and a bounded timeout. The reference has no sequence number or response correlation; never continue a heater sequence after losing alignment.
troubleshooting.symptom: No response or responses appear to belong to another request.

setup.notes: No Wi-Fi provisioning, Anova account, cloud API, application key or fixed PIN appears in the official local client. Connect, subscribe to RX then ASYNC, and read the temperature unit before commands. Bonding remains unknown; see device.pairing. This flow has not been replayed on hardware.

rejoin.notes: There is no router to rejoin on this BLE path. Moving hosts means scanning and connecting from the new host; whether an old bond must be removed, and how, is unknown. No factory reset is asserted as necessary.

testing.notes: No Nano was scanned, connected, paired or driven by this project. Anova's official client and actual proto2 schema were exercised only with synthetic data and fake BLE objects in the research pack. The unified Android app's React Native bundle corroborates the service and all three characteristics, not COBS, protobuf opcodes or live compatibility. Independent standard- library framing and decode checks are in scripts/test_anova_precision_cooker_nano.py; vectors are not captures.

evidence.app_static_analysis: The November 15 follow-up checked the sibling-held unified app com.anovaculinary.android 3.6.6 (versionCode 2127). The Nano service and TX, RX and ASYNC UUIDs all occur in its React Native bundle. This supports the model's identifier map only. No opcode, COBS or protobuf claim is inferred from those strings.

evidence.documentation_review: Anova's Nano overview, BLE protocol, commands, API, protobuf and implementation pages were compared with the actual pinned MIT client and schema. The executable source is primary wherever the cached web tables conflict. evidence.open_questions: See remaining_unknowns. Start with read-only hardware captures of GATT, get_temperature_unit and get_sensors, then resolve response headers, ASYNC, pairing and timer semantics. Obtain the authentic manual and verify attended stop before any start or setpoint write.

initialization.notes: Open RX notifications first. Command responses are reassembled from this characteristic.
Open ASYNC second, as the official client does. Its payload schema is unknown; do not treat alert/message definitions as proof of the envelope.

initialization.description: A future dedicated client must send get_temperature_unit through its COBS encoder before interpreting or setting temperatures. This is deliberately not a raw initialization write: the logical 00 07 packet must be COBS-framed first.

DeviceInfo.description: Schema-only message, not a declared read response: uint32 revision, modelNumber, boardRevision, bom, platform, cmCode and dateCode at fields 1-7, followed by string serialNumber at field 8. The reference client does not implement its read; never publish a real serial.

DeviceState.description: Schema-only message with required SensorValue waterTemp field 1 and SysAlertBitVector alerts field 2. The web page's flat DeviceStatus and CookingState definitions are absent from the actual schema. ASYNC transport of this message is unverified.

FirmwareInfo.description: Proto2 fields: string commitId field 1, string tagId field 2, uint32 dateCode field 3.
parse_rules: Parse length-delimited strings with bounds checks and a bounded uint32 varint. Do not search for the first 0x0a as a universal header-stripping rule.
Expose dateCode as a raw integer unless firmware evidence confirms the reference client's assumed Unix-timestamp interpretation.

IntegerValue.description: Proto2 message with required signed int32 value as field 1: tag 0x08 followed by a protobuf base-128 varint. It is not fixed-width little-endian. Command meanings and units come from the request's domain/type header.
IntegerValue.example: 00 03 08 8f 05 = domain 0, type 3, IntegerValue.value 655 (65.5 in the current unit)

fields.description: Signed int32 at field 1. Non-negative command values use ordinary unsigned LEB128; standard int32 negative values use sign-extended protobuf encoding, which this spec's non-negative UI parameters do not emit.
fields.name: value

parse_rules: Strictly COBS-decode after removing the frame delimiter, then separate the two-byte domain/type header from the proto2 body only after validating the expected response shape.
Require field tag 0x08 for IntegerValue and consume the complete varint with bounds checks. Reject truncated/overlong encodings and unexpected trailing fields rather than returning zero.
For target temperature use raw x 0.1 in the current unit. For the timer use raw minutes. For unit selection interpret raw as UnitType, not temperature.

SensorValueList.description: Proto2 repeated field 1 of SensorValue entries. Each list entry is a length-delimited SensorValue with required int32 value field 1 (tag 08), UnitType units field 2 (tag 10), and sensorType field 3 (tag 18).
SensorValueList.example: 00 05 0a 07 08 8f 05 10 00 18 00 = one water-temperature sensor, raw 655, units 0, sensorType 0 = 65.5 C

fields.description: Zero or more complete SensorValue entries. Preserve ordering, raw values, units and sensor types; do not expose only the first temperature.
fields.name: values

parse_rules: For the expected get_sensors response require header 00 05 before parsing the list. Other response headers are not silently accepted as this shape.
Parse each length-delimited entry within its declared boundary and require all three fields. Unknown wire types, units and sensor types remain explicit errors/unknowns.
Temperature conversions use protocol_details.unit_types: raw/10 for units 0 or 1, raw/100 for 4 or 5, and raw unchanged for 6 or 7. Motor speed and Boolean are not temperatures.
Water temperature is sensorType 0 only. A missing water sensor is unknown, never zero; do not copy the reference client's unknown-unit Fahrenheit fallback.

SysAlertBitVector.description: Required uint32 prevSetVector field 1 and currVector field 2. Flag meanings are bit masks, not list indices; previous/current and transport semantics are unverified.
parse_rules: Do not decode arbitrary ASYNC bytes as this message until a capture establishes the envelope. Surface safety bits if later confirmed; never use them to suppress or override device protections.

protocol_details.error_envelope: The schema defines MessageError values 0-8 but neither the web pages nor the client defines how errors are encapsulated or correlated with requests. Do not reinterpret a returned IntegerValue as one of these errors without a capture.

excluded_operations.bulk_domain: Domain 1 page/file/erase/reset operations are excluded, including firmware transfer and system reset.
excluded_operations.reason: The schema contains additional power, sound, display, timer-control, connection-parameter, device-info, alert and message-spoof IDs, plus a separate bulk-transfer domain with page/file/reset operations. The reference client does not implement or validate these paths. No bytes for them are offered as commands here.
excluded_operations.state_and_alerts: ASYNC, DeviceState and alert vectors are schema candidates only; no live state machine is claimed.

logical_commands.description: Documentary pre-COBS domain/type/proto2 forms for the commands above. packet_hex and packet_parts are retained for independent tests and future dedicated-client authors; they are deliberately outside the generic BLE command executor. command_vectors below contains the correct final bytes after transport.encode_steps, not bytes to emit from the logical form.

transport.command_template_boundary: TX.commands entries are documentary only and deliberately carry no executable value/template fields or entity bindings. The logical packet forms below are not generic-consumer encoding instructions: no anova_nano_cobs handler exists. A future dedicated client must perform the following steps. Writing any logical packet without those steps is a client bug, including start and stop.
decode_steps: Accumulate RX chunks in arrival order. The source heuristic completes a response when a chunk is shorter than 20 bytes OR ends in 0x00; bound total size and time because the heuristic is not a validated general fragmentation protocol.

Remove the transport delimiter before applying a strict COBS decoder. Reject malformed codes, truncation and excess data. Do not copy the reference decoder's permissive full-delimiter behavior, which can add a trailing zero.
Validate the response header and expected proto2 body for the one request in flight. Do not strip headers by searching for 0x08, 00 05 or the first 0x0a anywhere in the body.
Serialize requests with a timeout and stale-frame rejection. No request ID, command lock or universal response domain/type correlation is documented.
encode_steps: Build the two-byte domain/type header and append the exact proto2 payload, if any. Normal commands use domain 0.
COBS-encode the entire header-plus-payload using standard consistent-overhead-byte-stuffing code blocks, including long blocks of 254 non-zero bytes.
Append exactly one 0x00 frame delimiter. COBS supplies framing, not a checksum or authentication.
Split the encoded frame INCLUDING its delimiter into consecutive chunks of at most 20 bytes and write them in order to TX. Twenty is the source chunk size, not a negotiated-MTU prohibition.
transport.logical_packet: [one-byte domain][one-byte message type][zero or more proto2 payload bytes]
transport.response_vector_note: The published command vectors are exact source-generated offline vectors. The response vector below is synthetic and independently transcribed from the actual proto2 field definitions, not a cooker capture.

remaining_unknowns: Actual firmware acceptance of the executable schema's domain/opcode map over the conflicting web tables, plus complete GATT properties and required TX write mode.
Response headers, request/response correlation, RX short-chunk termination, timeout behavior, MTU negotiation and malformed-frame handling.
ASYNC payload envelope and whether DeviceState/SysAlertBitVector is actually transported; no reliable cooking state machine is known.
Pairing, bonding, central/bond limits, reconnect behavior, unpairing and physical factory reset. Do not inherit sibling procedures.
Authenticated manual electrical limits, safe temperature range, water/vessel requirements and regional-model differences; unused client constants are not promoted as limits.
Timer running/completion behavior, zero semantics, maximum and exact minutes behavior on firmware.
FirmwareInfo.dateCode semantics and the unimplemented DeviceInfo read/serial handling.
Error encapsulation and correlation for MessageError 0-8.
Bulk transfer, firmware update, reset, message spoof, additional settings and unattended-heating behavior are excluded and unverified.

get_cooking_timer.description: Domain 0, type 18 (0x12), empty payload, pre-COBS. Expected IntegerValue is minutes. Validate the response header; stop/cancel timer operations are not part of the demonstrated client subset. Documentary only; no executable value or entity binding.

get_firmware_info.description: Domain 0, type 26 (0x1a), empty payload, pre-COBS. Expected FirmwareInfo has commit ID, tag ID and uint32 date code. The client's Unix-timestamp interpretation of date code is not hardware-verified. Documentary only; no executable value or entity binding.

get_sensors.description: Domain 0, type 5, empty payload, pre-COBS. Expected SensorValueList response; preserve all sensors and apply each entry's own unit scale. It does not establish cooking state. Documentary only; no executable value or entity binding.

get_target_temperature.description: Domain 0, type 4, empty payload, pre-COBS. Expected IntegerValue response is raw tenths of a degree in the current unit; validate its response header instead of assuming every response echoes type 4. Documentary only; no executable value or entity binding.

get_temperature_unit.description: Domain 0, type 7, empty payload, pre-COBS. Required before temperature interpretation. Expected IntegerValue carries a UnitType; 0/4/6 mean C and 1/5/7 mean F for display, with scale 10/100/1 respectively. Documentary only; no executable value or entity binding.

set_cooking_timer.description: Domain 0, type 16 (0x10), IntegerValue field 1 containing MINUTES, pre-COBS. The executable method, README and prompts agree on minutes; the source-file top comment saying seconds is wrong. Zero semantics, maximum and running-timer behavior are unknown. Documentary only; no executable template or entity binding.

minutes.description: Non-negative whole minutes encoded as unsigned protobuf varint. No maximum is asserted; do not assign disabled/unlimited meaning to zero without device evidence.

set_target_temperature.advanced_reason: Changing the target can heat an active bath, and the same number means different temperatures in C and F. Read the current unit and confirm physical setup with the owner present; read target/sensors afterwards and keep stop_cooking documented for recovery by a dedicated client. This command has no generic action binding.
set_target_temperature.description: Domain 0, type 3, IntegerValue field 1. The UI parameter is the raw signed-scale numerator: raw = truncate-toward-zero(temperature x 10), in the current unit. The logical packet parts are pre-COBS. This declared varint form accepts non-negative raw values only; negative int32 encoding and any safe operating range are outside this spec.

setpoint.description: Non-negative raw tenths of a degree in the current unit (65.5 becomes 655). UnitTypes 0/4/6 map to C and 1/5/7 to F, while setpoint scale remains 0.1. A future dedicated encoder truncates temperature x 10 toward zero and emits unsigned protobuf varint; no safe maximum is asserted.

set_temperature_unit.description: Domain 0, type 6, IntegerValue field 1: 0 selects 0.1 C and 1 selects 0.1 F, pre-COBS. Read the unit and all temperatures afterwards; do not interpret any other input as Fahrenheit. Documentary only; no executable template or entity binding.

unit.description: UnitType enum value placed in IntegerValue.value. The reference client uses only 0 and 1 for writes.

start_cooking.advanced_reason: This can start an immersion heater. Confirm the unit, setpoint, timer and physical setup with the owner present. No validated cooking-state response exists here, so stop immediately on any unexpected result and do not treat a raw acknowledgment as success. There is deliberately no generic action binding for this command.
start_cooking.description: Domain 0, type 10 (0x0a), empty payload, pre-COBS. The reference sets a local flag after any raw response; that is not evidence of actual heating. Confirm state through real responses once a capture establishes them. No generic turn_on binding exists: advanced confirmation and outcome-unknown semantics require a dedicated UI. Stop remains documented separately, not a success proof.

stop_cooking.description: Domain 0, type 11 (0x0b), empty payload, pre-COBS. Ordinary recovery command, deliberately not advanced and not exposed as a generic turn_off action. A raw response, cleared local flag or write result does not prove the heater stopped.

characteristics.name: TX (host to cooker)
characteristics.notes: The official client writes sequential chunks of at most 20 bytes with no explicit response argument, so the exact hardware property set and required ATT write mode were not established. Both write modes are listed as candidates, not as a claim that every unit exposes both. Discover actual properties and follow the reference's default behavior rather than forcing response=False. No generic COBS handler exists: these commands are documentary and have no executable byte fields or entity bindings. A future dedicated encoder must frame every logical packet in protocol_details.logical_commands before writing.

characteristics.name: RX (cooker responses)
characteristics.notes: Subscribe before commands. Reassemble notification chunks with the bounded source heuristic in protocol_details.transport, remove the delimiter before strict COBS decode, then parse the two-byte header and expected proto2 payload. No sequence number or universal response-type echo is established; serialize requests and reject stale responses.

characteristics.name: ASYNC (unsolicited cooker data)
characteristics.notes: Subscribe after RX, but the reference handler only logs raw chunks. DeviceState and alert messages in the schema are capture candidates, not proven ASYNC payloads. No cooking state, alert bit or notification envelope is decoded or exposed as fact here.

services.name: Anova Precision Cooker Nano control
services.notes: UUIDs come from Anova's Nano source and are corroborated in the unified app bundle. Commands declared on TX are documentary descriptions of logical packets BEFORE COBS, held in protocol_details.logical_commands rather than executable value/template fields. RX responses use the same outer framing, but their header/payload correlation is not fully established and must be checked per the expected request.
